mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the previous month signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI annualized growth > 2% does not correlate with negative SPX returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the previous three months signals a tightening labor market, which leads to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or UNRATE decrease > 0.5pp does not correlate with positive SPX returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (RSAFS) over the previous three months signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of instances despite the positive signal, or RSAFS growth does not correlate with positive SPX returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous month signals increased economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increase > 1% does not correlate with positive SPX returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) annualized growth is below 1%, it signals a potential monetary policy misalignment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL < 1% does not correlate with negative SPX returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 over the previous month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3 percentage points, it signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200k and UNRATE decreases > 0.3pp in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction of PAYEMS increase > 200k and UNRATE decrease > 0.3pp does not correlate with positive SPX returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Housing Starts (HOUST) by more than 10% over the previous two months signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or HOUST decrease > 10% does not correlate with negative SPX returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When Real GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative for two consecutive quarters and Industrial Production (INDPRO) decreases by more than 2% over the same period, it signals a recessionary environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 negative for 2 quarters and INDPRO decreases > 2%
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of negative GDPC1 growth and INDPRO decrease > 2% does not correlate with negative SPX returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).
